title: Looking for feedback on my 2D arena shooter – ArenaShooter
author: PlayL1keMe
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I'm working on a 2D arena shooter called **ArenaShooter**, and I'd really appreciate it if you could give it a try and share your thoughts!

  
**The main gameplay loop is simple:**

1. Level up and unlock upgrade cards.
2. Improve your damage, attack speed, HP, critical damage, critical chance, healing item drop chance, and healing item effectiveness.
3. Complete achievements to unlock new upgrade cards.

The game is still in early development, and there's not a huge amount of content yet. However, I'd love to hear your opinion on how the game feels to play. Is the gameplay enjoyable? Does the progression feel rewarding? What would you change or improve?

**A small note about localization:**

The upgrade cards haven't been translated into English yet, so I apologize for the inconvenience. I'm hoping the artwork on each card makes its purpose relatively intuitive even without reading the text.

You can check your upgrade cards and character stats at any time by pressing **I**, or by pressing **Esc** and selecting **Inventory**.

**You can play ArenaShooter here:**

[https://grindinglootgames.itch.io/arenashooter](https://grindinglootgames.itch.io/arenashooter)

Any feedback is welcome, whether it's about gameplay, balance, progression, visuals, or bugs.

Thanks a lot to everyone who takes the time to play! I'd be happy to read your thoughts.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/PlayL1keMe please add details on how AI was used to make this. Just stating that you used AI doesn't pass the rule. The community is a dev community, add dev details. Rule 4 is there to make sure promotional posts contribute by getting into the process and actual development. There's a real risk of the sub being swamped by self-promotion. If you don't update, this post may be removed.

comments.author: VortexAssetStudio
comments.body: Congrats on getting a playable prototype out! Making the card artwork intuitive enough to understand without reading text is actually a great design goal, especially for fast-paced arena shooters where you don't want to break the flow.When you're iterating on those card icons, keeping the silhouettes distinct and using strong color coding for different stat types (like red/orange for damage vs green for healing drops) usually helps players recognize them in a split second. Best of luck with the Godot build, looking forward to seeing how the meta-progression evolves!
